title: Homotopy invariance of enriched coends with one projectively cofibrant variable
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, weak homotopy equivalences and universes of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and enriched projective diagram model structures of [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus]. Let $A$ be a small simplicial category. A left module is an enriched functor $H:A\to\mathsf{sSet}$ and a right module is an enriched functor $V:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$. Define $V\otimes_A H$ to be the coequalizer of the action maps
$$\coprod_{a,b}V(b)\times A(a,b)\times H(a)\rightrightarrows\coprod_a V(a)\times H(a).$$
For $B=A$ or $A^{\mathrm{op}}$, an enriched diagram $B\to\mathsf{sSet}$ is projectively cofibrant if and only if its initial map is a retract of a transfinite composite, continuous at limit stages, of pushouts of coproducts of $B(b,-)\times\partial\Delta^k\to B(b,-)\times\Delta^k$, with $k\geq0$. If $H$ is projectively cofibrant, every objectwise weak homotopy equivalence $V\to V'$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence $V\otimes_AH\to V'\otimes_AH$. If $V$ is projectively cofibrant, every objectwise weak homotopy equivalence $H\to H'$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence $V\otimes_AH\to V\otimes_AH'$. No cofibrancy or fibrancy hypothesis on the varying modules, and no local Kan hypothesis on $A$, is required.

source.place: A.3.3.2 and Remark A.3.3.5 (printed pp.870–871): free projective generators; agent coend cell/gluing consequence. Read online; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this enriched result.

proof.text: Work first with any small simplicial category $B$, covering both $A$ and $A^{\mathrm{op}}$. The Kan model category of simplicial sets is combinatorial and simplicial for its Cartesian enrichment by [lem-coef-simplicial-presheaf-projective-model]. Hence [lem-coef-simplicial-projective-model-calculus] gives the projective model structure on enriched $B$-diagrams, its local presentability and the free adjunction $F_bK=B(b,-)\times K\dashv\operatorname{ev}_b$. Put $I_B=\{F_b(\partial\Delta^k)\to F_b(\Delta^k):b\in\operatorname{Ob}B,\ k\geq0\}$. Transposing a square against such a map gives exactly a square against $\partial\Delta^k\to\Delta^k$ at $b$. By the boundary characterization in [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], $I_B^{\square}$ is precisely the objectwise trivial fibrations. Each map in $I_B$ is therefore a projective cofibration. All families are small in the fixed universe, enlarged if necessary.

source.place: A.3.3.2 and A.3.3.5, printed pp. 870–871: free projective generators; explicit boundary lifting test.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-presentable-cellular-factorization] to $I_B$ in the locally presentable diagram category of Step 1 and to $\varnothing\to P$. It factors as an initial $I_B$-cell map $\varnothing\to C$ followed by an objectwise trivial fibration $p:C\to P$. If $P$ is projectively cofibrant, its lifting property supplies $s:P\to C$ with $ps=1_P$, so its initial map is an arrow retract of the initial cell map. Conversely every such cell map has the left lifting property against objectwise trivial fibrations: at a successor choose a filler on each free boundary summand, extend across the pushout, and at a limit use the compatible fillers' colimit map. Start with the unique map from the initial diagram. Retracts retain the lifting property by [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. Thus a retract of an initial cell map is projectively cofibrant. This proves the stated characterization for both choices of $B$.

source.place: A.3.3.5, printed p. 871: explicit cellular factorization, transfinite lifting and retract argument.

proof.text: For a right $B$-module $Z$ and a left $B$-module $P$, use the displayed coequalizer in the item to form $Z\otimes_BP$. Colimits of enriched diagrams are objectwise: the action of $B(b,c)$ on a colimit is induced from the actions on its terms, since multiplication by a fixed simplicial set preserves colimits degreewise; the unit and associativity identities hold on every colimit leg. The same degreewise observation shows that $Z\otimes_B-$ preserves colimits: both coproducts in the coequalizer commute with a colimit in $P$, as do the coequalizer and that colimit. Explicitly a map out of either iterated colimit is the same compatible family of maps $Z(b)\times P_i(b)\to T$ satisfying the action equations. This also proves that the resulting isomorphisms commute with a morphism $Z\to Z'$ and with all attaching maps.

source.place: Agent coend calculation following A.3.3.5: colimit universal properties in simplicial sets.

proof.text: For every object $b$ and simplicial set $K$ there is a natural isomorphism $Z\otimes_BF_bK\cong Z(b)\times K$. In degree $r$ send the class of $(z,f,k)$, where $f\in B(b,c)_r$ and $z\in Z(c)_r$, to $(Z(f)z,k)$. The coend relation and associativity of the action make this well-defined. Its inverse sends $(z,k)$ to $[z,1_b,k]$, where the identity vertex is degenerated to degree $r$. One composite is the identity by the unit equation; the other is the identity because the relation identifies $[z,f,k]$ with $[Z(f)z,1_b,k]$. These formulas commute with simplicial operators, with maps of $Z$ and $K$, and with the inclusions of boundaries into simplices. In particular they identify the actual cell-attachment maps after applying the coend.

source.place: Agent enriched co-Yoneda calculation on the free diagrams of A.3.3.5; explicit mutually inverse maps.

proof.text: For any simplicial set $K$, multiplication by $K$ preserves weak homotopy equivalences. To check this without a fibrancy assumption, take a weak equivalence $f:X\to Y$. All simplicial sets are cofibrant by [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Apply [lem-coef-brown-split-factorizations] to obtain $f=pi$, $ps=1_Y$, where $i$ and $s$ are cofibrations and $p$ is a trivial fibration. Two-out-of-three makes both $i$ and $s$ weak equivalences, hence trivial cofibrations. In the Kan model structure trivial cofibrations are exactly the maps with the left lifting property against all Kan fibrations, that is, the anodyne maps. Applying [lem-coef-sset-anodyne-pushout-product] with the monomorphism $\varnothing\to K$ shows $K\times i$ and $K\times s$ anodyne, hence weak equivalences. Since $(K\times p)(K\times s)=1$, two-out-of-three makes $K\times p$ weak; composing with $K\times i$ proves the assertion. The factor exchange gives the same assertion for $-\times K$.

source.place: Agent product calculation from the Kan model axioms and the cited anodyne pushout-product theorem, used in the A.3.3.5 cell argument.

proof.text: A coproduct of weak homotopy equivalences of simplicial sets is a weak homotopy equivalence, including the empty coproduct. Indeed the realization quotient in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] identifies the realization of a simplicial coproduct with the topological disjoint union of the realizations: the simplex relations never change the summand. Paths lie in one summand, so components are the disjoint union of the summands' component sets. Likewise a based cube, and any homotopy between based cubes, has connected domain and lies in the basepoint's summand. Thus its based homotopy groups and induced maps are precisely those of that summand. The empty case has empty component sets and no basepoints.

source.place: Agent elementary realization-quotient calculation for coproducts, in the cell argument following A.3.3.5.

proof.text:
Let $u:Z\to Z'$ be an objectwise weak equivalence of right $B$-modules. Let $P_\alpha$ be an initial free-boundary cell presentation, continuous at limits. Prove by transfinite induction that $u\otimes_B P_\alpha$ is a weak equivalence. At $\alpha=0$ both coends are empty, hence the map is the identity. At a successor, suppose $P_\alpha\to P_{\alpha+1}$ attaches cells indexed by a small set $T$, at objects $b_t$ and dimensions $k_t$. By Steps 3–4 the coend for $Z$ is the pushout of the span
$$Z\otimes_BP_\alpha\ \longleftarrow\ \coprod_{t\in T} Z(b_t)\times\partial\Delta^{k_t}\ \longrightarrow\ \coprod_{t\in T} Z(b_t)\times\Delta^{k_t},$$
and the same is true for $Z'$, with a commuting map of spans induced by $u$. The rightward arrows are degreewise injective since boundary inclusions are injective, including $k_t=0$. Steps 5–6 give weak equivalences on both coproduct terms; the induction hypothesis gives the third. The pushout clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences], with its monomorphism leg taken to be the rightward arrow, proves that the actual successor coend comparison is weak.

source.place: Agent transfinite successor step following the free generators in A.3.3.5; application of the cited simplicial-set gluing theorem.

proof.text: At a nonzero limit ordinal $\beta$, Step 3 identifies each coend on $P_\beta$ with the colimit of its coends on $P_\alpha$, $\alpha<\beta$, naturally in $Z$. The ordinal category $\{\alpha:\alpha<\beta\}$ is a small nonempty directed poset: the maximum of a finite nonempty set of its elements is still below $\beta$, and $0$ bounds the empty set. The filtered-colimit clause of [lem-coef-sset-gluing-filtered-equivalences] therefore applies to the preceding comparison diagram and proves the limit-stage comparison weak. Together with Step 7, this proves the comparison for every initial cell module, including presentations of length zero and successor length.

source.place: Agent transfinite limit step following A.3.3.5; the directed-colimit clause of the cited simplicial-set theorem.

proof.text: For a projectively cofibrant left $B$-module $P$, choose the cell module $C$ and maps $P\xrightarrow{s}C\xrightarrow{p}P$ of Step 2 with $ps=1$. Applying $Z\otimes_B-$ and $Z'\otimes_B-$, naturality in the left variable gives commutative squares exhibiting $u\otimes_BP$ as an arrow retract of $u\otimes_BC$. The latter is weak by Steps 7–8; weak equivalences are retract closed in the Kan model structure [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper]. Hence $u\otimes_BP$ is weak. This proves the first invariance claim on taking $B=A$, $P=H$, and $u:V\to V'$.

source.place: Agent retract step following A.3.3.5 and the Kan model retract axiom.

proof.text: For the other invariance claim take $B=A^{\mathrm{op}}$, regard the projectively cofibrant right $A$-module $V$ as a left $B$-module, and regard $H\to H'$ as a map of right $B$-modules. Step 9 gives a weak equivalence $H\otimes_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}V\to H'\otimes_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}V$. Switching the two factors on every coproduct term induces an isomorphism $H\otimes_{A^{\mathrm{op}}}V\cong V\otimes_AH$: a relation between $[H(f)h,v]$ and $[h,V(f)v]$ becomes precisely the relation between $[v,H(f)h]$ and $[V(f)v,h]$. Switching again is the inverse. This is simplicial and natural in both modules, so it identifies the weak equivalence with the comparison asserted in the item. Every use of gluing involved only degreewise monomorphisms and every product argument allowed arbitrary simplicial sets; no local Kan condition on $A$ or cofibrancy or fibrancy of the varying modules has entered.

source.place: Agent opposite-category symmetry of the defining coequalizer, completing the cell/gluing consequence of A.3.3.5.
